{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that individuals with PTSD would exhibit impaired inhibitory control over memory retrieval compared to trauma-exposed control participants, resulting in reduced suppression-induced forgetting of aversive scenes.",
  "design": "mixed, with group (PTSD vs. control) as a between-subjects factor and condition (baseline vs. suppress) as a within-subjects factor.",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "The Think/No-Think (TNT) task, where participants were instructed to either recall or suppress memories of previously studied aversive object-scene pairs.",
  "outcome_measure": "Memory performance for scenes (identification, gist, and details) measured by the number of correct details recalled during a final test phase.",
  "population_and_setting": "18 individuals with a current diagnosis of PTSD and 18 trauma-exposed control individuals recruited from the local community and departmental participant panels.",
  "sample_size_total": 36,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Recruited through print advertisements from the local community and departmental participant panels.",
  "analysis_plan": "Mixed analysis of variance (ANOVA) with condition (baseline, suppress) as a within-subjects factor and group (PTSD, control) and set assignment as between-subject factors.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "Participants were native English speakers with no history of severe head injury, neurological disease, or learning disability. PTSD participants were excluded if they had a current diagnosis of psychosis or borderline personality disorder. Control participants were excluded if they had any current psychiatric disorder."
}
